figures.caption: Fig. 8: Curriculum warmup schedules for KL and diffusion losses. Delayed introduction of Ldiff (starts epoch 9) allows the encoder to stabilize before the diffusion prior begins shaping the latent space.

Fig. 6: NOTEARS modality importance weights wm over training epochs. The network initially over-weights Video (FACET facial AUs), then shifts to balance Text and Audio as fine-grained class boundaries become important.

Fig. 7: Training loss components over epochs for the Full Model. Vertical dotted lines mark the start and end of the diffusion warmup schedule. The task loss dominates; diffusion and KL terms are secondary regularizers.

Fig. 12: Affect-Diff performance on emotion recognition (3,292 samples) vs. sentiment analysis (22K samples). With 5× more training data and BERT features, balanced accuracy rises from 0.384 to 0.729 (7-class) and 0.925 (binary), directly quantifying the data-scale bottleneck.

Fig. 9: Val-BalAcc vs. parameter count (log scale). AffectDiff (Full) occupies the upper-right Pareto frontier: highest bal-BalAcc at its parameter scale. Baselines cluster at lower parameter counts and lower balanced accuracy.

Fig. 10: Validation balanced accuracy for three random seeds. All three runs converge to the same peak (0.384) at the same epoch (28), demonstrating stable training dynamics independent of initialization.

Fig. 4: Validation balanced accuracy over training. Full Model reaches the highest peak (0.384, epoch 28). All ablations and baselines converge strictly below the full model. The diffusion prior and stop-gradient jointly account for the largest gap.
